How did you handle a new routine?
I adapted to my new school by joining the music club.
Keep the past tense and the music club; do not force the base form adapt.
My teacher gave me an advice about choosing a university.
Correct the countability of advice without inventing the advice.
I borrowed my friend a book last week.
The intended direction is ambiguous; explain borrow/lend without asserting who owned the book.
I care about housing because many students cannot afford rent.
Do not invent political views or force a partisan opinion.
Correct subject-verb agreement; preserve the noise and sleep.
Going to bed earlier has had a good effect on my mood.
Do not replace correct effect with affect.
What did you learn at work?
I have many experience working with children.
Distinguish much experience from individual experiences; preserve work with children.
How did you solve a group problem?
We discussed about the deadline after class.
Remove about after discuss; do not alter the deadline.
I suggest to open the library earlier.
Offer suggest opening or suggest that it open; preserve earlier opening.
Why do you take the MRT?
It is convenient for me because the station is near my home.
This is natural English; do not insist on a different adjective.
Would you try a difficult activity?
Although it was raining, but we went hiking.
Remove the redundant but or restructure without changing the event.
How long have you lived here?
I have lived in Taipei since three years.
Use for three years, not a fabricated starting date.
What was hard about your new job?
I am used to wake up early now.
Use waking after be used to; do not confuse it with a discontinued past habit.
I prefer cycling to taking the bus.
Accept the parallel gerunds and preference.
We need two new equipments for our club.
Use two new pieces of equipment without inventing which devices.
The night market was fun, and I would go again.
Do not replace fun with funny; keep the willingness to return.
I study at a quiet cafe near the station.
Do not confuse quiet and quite or invent the station name.
How did you help a friend?
I lent my umbrella to a friend yesterday.
Preserve lent as the valid past tense of lend.
How did you feel about the class?
I was interesting in the history class.
Use interested for the learner's feeling; preserve history.
What did the guide give you?
The guide gave us useful information about the trail.
Do not add an article to uncountable information.
Students can raise their hands when they have questions.
Do not replace transitive raise with rise.
What do you do before leaving?
I always remember locking the door before I leave.
Remember doing versus remember to do changes meaning; avoid declaring the sentence impossible.
What did you do last summer?
I travelled to Tainan with my sister.
Accept British spelling travelled; do not invent transport or duration.
My family are very supportive of my decision.
Accept British collective-noun agreement; do not enforce only American usage.
How do you help at home?
I help my mother cook dinner on Sundays.
Both help cook and help to cook are valid; preserve Sundays.
How did you adjust to a new place?
剛搬來的時候有點不習慣，現在已經慢慢適應了。
Preserve natural Taiwan wording and the gradual change.
Who helped you make a decision?
老師給了我一些建議，讓我比較知道怎麼選。
Do not impose English countability rules on Chinese 建議.
Chinese 借 can be ambiguous; do not invent the lending direction.
我比較關心房租，因為學生的負擔真的很重。
Do not invent political opinions to force the target word.
樓上的聲音太大，影響到我的睡眠。
Accept conversational Taiwan Chinese and preserve the upstairs noise.
早一點睡之後，我白天的精神好多了，效果很明顯。
Do not invent medical claims or sleep durations.
What did your part-time job teach you?
這份打工讓我累積了很多和客人溝通的經驗。
打工 is natural Taiwan usage; do not replace it merely for formality.
How did your group plan its work?
下課後我們討論了一下分工。
Preserve the brevity; do not force English sentence length.
Why do you take the MRT?
我家離捷運站很近，所以搭捷運很方便。
Use 捷運, not a forced mainland synonym.
Would you go out in the rain?
雖然在下雨，但是我們還是出門了。
雖然 and 但是 together are valid Chinese, unlike English although/but.
How long have you lived in Taipei?
我在台北已經住三年了。
Accept this natural word order and do not invent the year of arrival.
What changed after you started work?
現在我已經習慣早起了。
Do not overcorrect a natural short sentence.
How do you prefer to commute?
比起搭公車，我比較喜歡騎腳踏車。
腳踏車 and 公車 are appropriate Taiwan terms.
社團需要添購兩台設備，但還沒決定買哪一種。
Do not invent a device type; Chinese classifiers need not mirror English countability.
昨天逛夜市很有趣，下次還想再去。
Preserve informal Taiwan style and the desire to return.
Where do you like to study?
我喜歡去車站附近那間安靜的咖啡廳讀書。
Do not invent a cafe name or location.
我對歷史很有興趣，尤其喜歡聽老師說故事。
Preserve the speaker's interest rather than saying history is objectively easy.
What did the guide give you?
導遊給了我們一些步道的資料。
Do not change the recipient or invent safety advice.
有問題的話可以先舉手。
Accept subject omission in natural Chinese.
What do you do before leaving?
Do not force an explicit subject or unnecessary tense markers.
What did you do last summer?
去年暑假我和姊姊去台南旅行。
姊姊 is a valid Taiwan spelling; do not force 姐姐.
家人都很支持我的決定。
Do not add a reason or a career choice.
How do you help at home?
我星期天會幫媽媽煮晚餐。
Helping can be expressed with 幫, not necessarily the entire target 幫忙.
因為公車晚到，所以我遲到了。
因為 and 所以 together are natural Chinese; do not apply English because/so rules.
What is your friend doing now?
正在 precedes the location here naturally; do not invent who 他 refers to.
